title: Motion for Leave to Answer and Answer of the Alaska Commercial Fisheries Conservation Alliance to DeepGreen Cook Inlet SPV LLC's supplemental clarification re Turbine Array Optimization, Footprint Reduction, and Environmental Spacing under P-15423.

documents.name: ACFCA_Motion_for_Leave_and_Answer_to_Supplemental_Clarification.pdf
documents.text:
UNITED STATES OF AMERICA
                                  BEFORE THE
                    FEDERAL ENERGY REGULATORY COMMISSION

DeepGreen Cook Inlet SPV, LLC                                      Docket No. P-15423-000
DeepGreen Cook Inlet Subsea-Compute and
Infrastructure Hub Project


             MOTION FOR LEAVE TO ANSWER AND ANSWER OF THE
          ALASKA COMMERCIAL FISHERIES CONSERVATION ALLIANCE
                 TO THE SUPPLEMENTAL CLARIFICATION OF
                     DEEPGREEN COOK INLET SPV LLC

       Pursuant to Rules 212 and 213 of the Commission's Rules of Practice and Procedure, 18
C.F.R. §§ 385.212 and 385.213, the Alaska Commercial Fisheries Conservation Alliance
("ACFCA"), a party to this proceeding, moves for leave to answer the Supplemental Clarification
of Applicant DeepGreen Cook Inlet SPV LLC Regarding Turbine Array Optimization, Footprint
Reduction, and Environmental Spacing, dated November 2, 2026 ("Supplemental Clarification"),
and submits this Answer.

I. MOTION FOR LEAVE TO ANSWER

        ACFCA filed its Motion to Intervene and Protest on September 14, 2026 (Submission IDs
1791000 and 1791227) and its Motion for Leave to Answer and Reply Comments on September
21, 2026 (Submission ID 1792347). ACFCA represents Upper Cook Inlet commercial set gillnet
and drift gillnet permit holders who fish in the East Foreland Corridor.

        The Supplemental Clarification is dated November 2, 2026, the last day of the intervention
and comment period set by the Notice of Preliminary Permit Application, 91 Fed. Reg. 56,879
(Sept. 4, 2026). No party could answer it within that period. It changes the project design described
in the application, including the number of turbines, their rating, the foundation type, the spacing,
and the footprint, and the record should be accurate on those points before the Commission acts. No
preliminary permit has issued, and DeepGreen made filings on October 27 and again on November
2, so a response filed within days of the second filing should not prejudice anyone. If the
Commission regards this filing as late, ACFCA asks it to accept the filing under Rule 2008(b), 18
C.F.R. § 385.2008(b), because the information it answers arrived on the final day. This Answer
addresses the Supplemental Clarification and the related statements in DeepGreen's Consolidated
Answer of October 27, 2026.




              ACFCA | FERC Docket No. P-15423-000 | Motion for Leave to Answer and Answer | Page 1
 II. BACKGROUND

        The application, filed February 11, 2026 and supplemented June 26, 2026, describes about
330 to 350 marine hydrokinetic turbines, 66 subsea data center pods, and a 3.5-mile, 115-kilovolt
cable to a landing in the Nikiski Industrial Corridor. The project area is about 1,650 acres in water
45 to 166 feet deep. The Commission's notice describes estimated annual generation of 100
megawatts, mostly to power the data center, with any surplus delivered to the Railbelt grid.
ACFCA's September 14 protest asked the Commission to require "specific turbine counts, power
ratings, and physical dimensions" for all turbines and pods.

        The Supplemental Clarification states that the project's "nominal 90 MW to 100 MW study
capacity is achievable with an array of approximately 60 to 70 units," that about 66 turbines
"provides 99 MW of nameplate capacity," and that the change "eliminates approximately 75% to
80% of the individual nacelle structures previously contemplated." DeepGreen presents the filing
as a correction of "factual mischaracterizations regarding turbine density and array footprint."

III. ANSWER
   A. Project design
         The count of 330 to 350 turbines appears in the Commission's own notice of the
application, 91 Fed. Reg. at 56,879. DeepGreen's own statement that the new array removes 75 to
80 percent of the structures "previously contemplated" shows the earlier design was DeepGreen's.
ACFCA asked for a turbine count and unit rating and is glad to have both. The filing still gives no
rotor diameter, hub height, minimum water depth, foundation dimensions, or project boundary, and
it offers a range of 60 to 70 units and a "study capacity" in place of a fixed design.

        ACFCA asks the Commission to direct DeepGreen to state its baseline design. ACFCA
also asks the Commission to decide whether the filing amends the application under 18 C.F.R. §
4.35, which provides for new public notice of a material amendment. Section 4.35(f)(2) defines a
material amendment to a preliminary permit application by reference to powerhouse location and
reservoir size, which do not describe a hydrokinetic array, so the Commission may need to decide
how the section applies here.
   B. Power supply
       Sixty-six turbines rated at 1.5 megawatts add up to 99 megawatts of nameplate capacity,
which is the maximum output at peak current. Average delivered power is lower. The study
Evaluating the Impact of Tidal Energy in the Cook Inlet on Alaska's Railbelt Electrical Grid,
prepared by the National Renewable Energy Laboratory (now the National Laboratory of the
Rockies), used a 41 percent capacity factor in its 200 megawatt example. ACFCA does not claim



              ACFCA | FERC Docket No. P-15423-000 | Motion for Leave to Answer and Answer | Page 2
 that figure applies at East Foreland. Applied to 99 megawatts, it would give an average near 40
megawatts, compared with the 100 megawatts of generation the application says would serve
mainly the data center.

        Mixed semidiurnal tides in Upper Cook Inlet produce up to four zero-velocity slack periods
a day, as ACFCA explained in its September 14 protest. Turbine output falls to zero then, and
passive cooling stops with it. The Supplemental Clarification does not say how the data center
would be powered through those periods, whether by battery storage, load management, or grid
supply, and ACFCA has not found that in the application. DeepGreen's October 27 Consolidated
Answer says it has no "formal binding partnership, co-sponsorship, or executed interconnection
agreement" with the Alaska Energy Authority and describes its references to the Cook Inlet
PowerLink as "conceptual engineering alignments." The record therefore does not identify a
source of power for slack periods. ACFCA asks the Commission to direct DeepGreen to describe
how the project load would be served during each slack period and to state its expected capacity
factor and annual energy output.
   C. Rotor size and water depth
         The Supplemental Clarification gives lateral turbine spacing of 2.5 to 3.5 rotor diameters,
"approximately 50 to 70 meters." Dividing 50 by 2.5 and 70 by 3.5 each gives a rotor diameter of
20 meters, about 66 feet. The rotor of the turbine DeepGreen names is reported at 18 meters, about
59 feet. The application places the project in water 45 to 166 feet deep. A rotor of 59 to 66 feet does
not fit in 45 feet of water, and any installation needs further clearance above the seabed and below
vessel keels. ACFCA asks the Commission to direct DeepGreen to state the rotor diameter, hub
height, required clearances, and minimum installation depth, and to say whether the array would be
limited to the deeper part of the corridor and how that would change the footprint and the fishing
grounds it occupies.
   D. Turbine model
        The Supplemental Clarification refers to "the commercially validated Andritz Hydro
HS1500 nacelle or equivalent utility-scale architecture." The Pacific Northwest National
Laboratory's Tethys database lists the Andritz Hydro Hammerfest HS1500, rated at 1.5 megawatts
with an 18 meter rotor, among the turbines at the MeyGen tidal project in Scotland, where three
Andritz units operate in water 31 to 38 meters deep. ACFCA does not dispute that the HS1500
exists. Three units at one Scottish site is a narrow record on which to call the design validated for
Upper Cook Inlet, with its ice, silt load, and tidal range. ACFCA asks the Commission to direct
DeepGreen to identify the manufacturer, model, rated power, and rotor diameter of its baseline




              ACFCA | FERC Docket No. P-15423-000 | Motion for Leave to Answer and Answer | Page 3
 turbine, the number of units in service and their years of operation, and the basis for calling the
design "commercially validated" for Cook Inlet conditions.
   E. Footprint and consultation
        The Supplemental Clarification says DeepGreen may "contract the total seabed boundary
footprint" or "maintain a wider study corridor," and it does not choose between them. It gives no
coordinates or acreage. It also says micro-siting and monitoring will be developed "in consultation
with" NMFS, the Alaska Department of Fish and Game, the Kenai Peninsula Borough, Alaska
Native Corporations and Tribes, "and commercial fishing stakeholders." ACFCA is a commercial
fishing stakeholder and wishes to take part. A statement in a pleading does not bind DeepGreen
unless the Commission makes it a condition of the permit.
   F. Permits and authorizations
        DeepGreen's October 27 Consolidated Answer says it "will secure all required permits and
comply with all applicable environmental protocols prior to commencing in-water work" and will
coordinate study methods with NMFS and ADF&G. Defenders of Wildlife has argued in this
docket that Endangered Species Act and Marine Mammal Protection Act review is required at the
permit stage, and ACFCA has raised the question with NOAA Fisheries. ACFCA does not ask the
Commission to resolve that question here. It asks that DeepGreen's stated commitments be written
into any permit.

IV. REQUESTED RELIEF

       ACFCA requests that the Commission:

   1. Grant leave to answer and accept this Answer into the record.

   2. Direct DeepGreen, within 30 days, to file a statement identifying (a) its baseline project
      design and turbine count; (b) the manufacturer, model, rated power, rotor diameter, and hub
      height of its baseline turbine; (c) the minimum water depth and clearances needed for
      installation; (d) the project boundary, with coordinates and acreage; (e) how project load
      would be served during each slack tide period, with its expected capacity factor and annual
      energy output; and (f) the identity of its owners and of any party with a right to control or
      acquire the project, and whether any agreement exists to sell, assign, or transfer the
      application, a permit, or the project site.

   3. Decide whether the Supplemental Clarification amends the application under 18 C.F.R. §
      4.35 and, if it does, issue new notice.




             ACFCA | FERC Docket No. P-15423-000 | Motion for Leave to Answer and Answer | Page 4
    4. Defer action on the preliminary permit until the statement in item 2 is filed and parties have
      had time to respond. If the Commission issues a permit sooner, ACFCA asks that it include
      these conditions: (a) DeepGreen files a consultation plan within 90 days that identifies how
      Upper Cook Inlet commercial fishing stakeholders, including ACFCA, will be consulted;
      (b) each progress report describes that consultation; (c) no in-water activity begins until all
      required federal and state authorizations are obtained; (d) each progress report documents
      DeepGreen's coordination with NMFS and ADF&G; (e) DeepGreen notifies the
      Commission and the parties within 30 days of any change in ownership or control, or any
      agreement to transfer the permit or project site, consistent with the rule that a preliminary
      permit is not transferable; and (f) each progress report states the studies completed and the
      milestones met toward a license application, so the Commission can judge diligence.

   5. Continue to serve ACFCA on the official service list.

Respectfully submitted,
